import { Backpack, Boxes, Braces, RadioTower, ReceiptText, Search, Send, ShieldCheck, TriangleAlert } from 'lucide-react';

Connect Backpack in a React app, read native GOR balance, send a wallet-signed transaction, and link the result to the explorer.

These examples use Next.js App Router, `@solana/wallet-adapter-react`, and `@solana/web3.js`. The same provider and hook pattern works in other React apps. This page uses wallet adapter plus `web3.js` because those APIs match many existing Solana browser apps.

## Before you start

You need:

- Backpack installed and funded with native GOR
- Gorbagana RPC: `https://rpc.gorbagana.wtf`
- a React app that can render client components

<Callout type="info" title="Why wallet adapter">
  Backpack supports Solana wallet flows. Wallet adapter detects Wallet Standard wallets automatically, so the Gorbagana example does not need a Backpack-specific adapter package.
</Callout>

## Add wallet providers

Create `app/providers.tsx`.

```tsx
"use client";

import { type WalletError } from "@solana/wallet-adapter-base";
import { ConnectionProvider, WalletProvider } from "@solana/wallet-adapter-react";
import { WalletModalProvider } from "@solana/wallet-adapter-react-ui";
import "@solana/wallet-adapter-react-ui/styles.css";
import { type ReactNode, useCallback, useMemo } from "react";

const GORBAGANA_RPC_URL = "https://rpc.gorbagana.wtf";

export function Providers({ children }: { children: ReactNode }) {
  // Wallet Standard wallets, including Backpack, are detected automatically.
  const wallets = useMemo(() => [], []);

  const onError = useCallback((error: WalletError) => {
    console.error(error.name, error.message);
  }, []);

  return (
    <ConnectionProvider endpoint={GORBAGANA_RPC_URL}>
      <WalletProvider autoConnect onError={onError} wallets={wallets}>
        <WalletModalProvider>{children}</WalletModalProvider>
      </WalletProvider>
    </ConnectionProvider>
  );
}
```

Use a fixed Gorbagana RPC URL. Do not use `clusterApiUrl()` here because Gorbagana is not one of the built-in Solana clusters.

Wrap your app in `app/layout.tsx`.

```tsx
import { Providers } from "./providers";

export default function RootLayout({
  children,
}: Readonly<{ children: React.ReactNode }>) {
  return (
    <html lang="en">
      <body>
        <Providers>{children}</Providers>
      </body>
    </html>
  );
}
```

## Read native GOR balance

Use `useConnection` and `useWallet` to read the connected wallet balance.

```tsx
"use client";

import { useConnection, useWallet } from "@solana/wallet-adapter-react";
import { LAMPORTS_PER_SOL } from "@solana/web3.js";
import { useEffect, useState } from "react";

function formatGor(lamports: number) {
  return (lamports / LAMPORTS_PER_SOL).toLocaleString(undefined, {
    maximumFractionDigits: 9,
  });
}

export function WalletBalance() {
  const { connection } = useConnection();
  const { publicKey } = useWallet();
  const [balanceLamports, setBalanceLamports] = useState<number | null>(null);

  useEffect(() => {
    let cancelled = false;

    async function loadBalance() {
      if (!publicKey) {
        setBalanceLamports(null);
        return;
      }

      const lamports = await connection.getBalance(publicKey, "confirmed");

      if (!cancelled) {
        setBalanceLamports(lamports);
      }
    }

    loadBalance().catch(() => {
      if (!cancelled) setBalanceLamports(null);
    });

    return () => {
      cancelled = true;
    };
  }, [connection, publicKey]);

  if (!publicKey) return null;

  return (
    <p>
      {balanceLamports === null ? "Loading..." : `${formatGor(balanceLamports)} GOR`}
    </p>
  );
}
```

## Send a transaction

Use the connected wallet to sign and submit a small native GOR transfer.

```tsx
"use client";

import { WalletNotConnectedError } from "@solana/wallet-adapter-base";
import { useConnection, useWallet } from "@solana/wallet-adapter-react";
import {
  LAMPORTS_PER_SOL,
  PublicKey,
  SystemProgram,
  Transaction,
} from "@solana/web3.js";
import { useCallback, useState } from "react";

const GOR_AMOUNT = 0.001;

export function SendGorButton({
  recipientAddress,
}: {
  recipientAddress: string;
}) {
  const { connection } = useConnection();
  const { publicKey, sendTransaction } = useWallet();
  const [signature, setSignature] = useState<string | null>(null);
  const [error, setError] = useState<string | null>(null);
  const [isSending, setIsSending] = useState(false);

  const sendGor = useCallback(async () => {
    if (!publicKey) throw new WalletNotConnectedError();

    const recipient = new PublicKey(recipientAddress);
    const lamports = Math.round(GOR_AMOUNT * LAMPORTS_PER_SOL);

    const transaction = new Transaction().add(
      SystemProgram.transfer({
        fromPubkey: publicKey,
        toPubkey: recipient,
        lamports,
      }),
    );

    const {
      context: { slot: minContextSlot },
      value: { blockhash, lastValidBlockHeight },
    } = await connection.getLatestBlockhashAndContext("confirmed");

    transaction.feePayer = publicKey;
    transaction.recentBlockhash = blockhash;

    const txSignature = await sendTransaction(transaction, connection, {
      minContextSlot,
    });

    await connection.confirmTransaction(
      {
        blockhash,
        lastValidBlockHeight,
        signature: txSignature,
      },
      "confirmed",
    );

    setSignature(txSignature);
  }, [connection, publicKey, recipientAddress, sendTransaction]);

  const onClick = useCallback(async () => {
    setError(null);
    setIsSending(true);

    try {
      await sendGor();
    } catch (err) {
      setError(err instanceof Error ? err.message : "Transaction failed");
    } finally {
      setIsSending(false);
    }
  }, [sendGor]);

  return (
    <div>
      <button disabled={!publicKey || isSending} onClick={onClick} type="button">
        {isSending ? "Sending..." : "Send 0.001 GOR"}
      </button>

      {signature ? (
        <a
          href={`https://explorer.gorbagana.wtf/tx/${signature}`}
          rel="noreferrer"
          target="_blank"
        >
          Open in Explorer
        </a>
      ) : null}

      {error ? <p role="alert">{error}</p> : null}
    </div>
  );
}
```

`sendTransaction` asks the connected wallet to sign and submit through the Gorbagana connection. Rebuild the transaction if the blockhash expires.

If your app needs explicit signing before submission, check that `signTransaction` exists on `useWallet()` before calling it.

## UX checklist

Show these details before asking the user to sign:

| Item | Why |
| --- | --- |
| Network | Confirms the app is using Gorbagana RPC |
| Sender | Shows the connected wallet address |
| Recipient | Prevents accidental transfers |
| Amount | Shows native GOR amount before signing |
| Fee payer | Shows which wallet pays transaction fees |
| Explorer link | Gives the user a place to verify the result |

<Callout type="warn" title="Never put private keys in frontend code">
  Browser apps should ask wallets to sign transactions. Keep deployment keypairs and server keys out of client bundles.
</Callout>

## Common frontend issues

<Accordions type="single">
<Accordion title="Backpack does not appear">

Install or update Backpack, reload the page, and confirm the provider component renders on the client. Wallet Standard wallets are detected automatically, so `wallets={[]}` is valid for Backpack.

</Accordion>
<Accordion title="The app reads the wrong network">

Check the `ConnectionProvider` endpoint. It should be `https://rpc.gorbagana.wtf`. Show that network target in the UI before signing.

</Accordion>
<Accordion title="The transaction was signed but not found">

Search the exact signature in the explorer. If it does not appear, search the sender address, then rebuild the transaction with a fresh blockhash before retrying.

</Accordion>
<Accordion title="The wallet has no native GOR">

Search the connected Backpack address in the explorer. If the address has no native GOR, use the [Bridge](/network/bridge) before sending app transactions.

</Accordion>
</Accordions>

## Production checklist

Before shipping a frontend flow:

- show network, sender, recipient, amount, and fee payer
- use a fresh blockhash for each transaction attempt
- disable the submit button while a transaction is in progress
- show the transaction signature and explorer link after submission
- search the explorer before retrying a submitted transaction
- keep keypairs and private keys out of browser code
